correctness.rationale: A direct case proof establishes necessity and sufficiency. At least two omitted vertices from the nonattachment clique form a permanent fort. With zero omissions, the clique starts the path. With one omission and the attachment blue, another clique vertex clears the omission. With one omission and the attachment white, neither clique nor path can move unless the path contains its terminal endpoint or a consecutive selected pair; either pattern propagates to the attachment and then clears the graph. The disjoint cases give the polynomial. The packaged exhaustive checker independently confirms the criterion, coefficients, and minimum-set count for every tested pair through order \(14\).

value.rationale: The clique-path lollipop is a standard named family whose dense block and path tail create a genuine interface phenomenon. The theorem isolates that interface in a complete if-and-only-if rule, gives all polynomial coefficients in closed form, and classifies every minimum set. This is a natural infinite exact profile and is materially stronger than a minimum-number computation.
